open_points.subject: personal-data classification of project display names
open_points.text: “Personal data — the customer's contact and fiscal data and the object's address and identifying characteristics are `personal_data`” conflicts with R0-82: “the display name is held as `personal_data`.”
open_points.question: Is the project display name part of the `personal_data` class everywhere, including the actor/trust-boundary definition and operation disclosure rules?
options: Classify every project display name as `personal_data`
Classify only display names that actually contain identifying information as `personal_data`
open_points.default_guess: Classify every project display name as `personal_data`, as R0-82 explicitly requires.

open_points.subject: external language-model provider
open_points.text: The Agent is “any language-model agent acting for the owner,” while the exclusions mention “the external AI providers,” but no provider or provider boundary is defined among the actors and trust boundaries.
open_points.question: What external system runs the language model, what Registry-derived data may it receive through the agent, and which guarantees stop at that boundary?
options: Model providers are external processors that receive every agent-visible value
The model is entirely owner-hosted and no external provider receives agent-visible values
Both arrangements are supported with different trust boundaries
open_points.default_guess: Treat any model provider as an external system outside Registry's guarantees that may receive all agent-visible outputs, but no field classified as `personal_data`.

open_points.subject: customer erasure contents
open_points.text: “erase a customer's contact data” says “name, phone, e-mail and language are gone,” while also saying the Customer “keeps only its identity and the fact that it was erased”; fiscal data, kind, restriction state and relationship-end state are not reconciled.
open_points.question: Exactly which stored Customer facts are removed and which survive erasure, especially tax id, legal name, kind, restriction state, relationship-end date and revision?
options: Remove every fact except `customer_ref` and the erased marker
Remove contact and fiscal values but retain non-personal lifecycle facts
Remove only name, phone, e-mail and language
open_points.default_guess: Remove every fact except `customer_ref`, the erased marker and any structural revision required by the storage model.

open_points.subject: agent-session access version
open_points.text: “read the session's access” returns “the access version,” but no text says which actions increment it or whether idempotent, refused or request-only changes move it.
open_points.question: When does the session access version change: registration, grant, revoke, active-project change or clear, request creation or replacement, request answer, project erasure, project archiving, and idempotent replays?
options: Increment for every accepted mutation of session access or its pending request
Increment only when the granted set or active project changes
Maintain separate versions for access and pending requests
open_points.default_guess: Increment one access version for every accepted change to the granted set, active project or pending request, but not for refused or no-op replays.

open_points.subject: audit coverage of state-changing actions
open_points.text: R0-58 records “only significant changes of state: changes to projects and customer records, granting and revoking an agent session's projects, restricting processing and lifting it, and erasures and anonymisations,” without deciding whether room and artifact changes, session registration, active-project changes, access requests and answers, import, or audit-log erasure are included.
open_points.question: Which exact primary actions produce audit entries?
options: Audit every accepted state-changing primary action
Audit only the actions expressly enumerated in R0-58
Audit the enumerated actions plus a separately declared security-sensitive subset
open_points.default_guess: Audit every accepted state-changing primary action except operations that R0-58 expressly excludes as ordinary agent calls or flow steps.

open_points.subject: audit entries for refused changes
open_points.text: R0-58 says the log records “changes of state,” but R0-37 says each audit entry includes “the outcome”; it is not stated whether refused attempts, which change no state, are logged.
open_points.question: Does the audit log contain refused attempts at significant changes, and if so which refusals?
options: Record only accepted changes, with outcome always successful
Record accepted and refused attempts for audited actions
Record only selected security-relevant refusals
open_points.default_guess: Record accepted changes only; authentication and other refused attempts belong to infrastructure security logging.

open_points.subject: personal data inside retained artifact pointers
open_points.text: R0-62 and R0-71 say an anonymised project keeps its artifact pointers and “holds no personal value,” while R0-68 says Registry does not inspect pointer values and a pointer that contains a prohibited name or address “is not refused and does reach the agent.”
open_points.question: What happens on anonymisation when a retained `uri`, `payload_ref` or digest may itself identify the customer or object?
options: Keep pointers unconditionally and weaken the claim that anonymisation leaves no personal value
Require the owner or governance review to establish that retained pointers are non-identifying before anonymisation
Remove or redact identifying pointer values during anonymisation
Refuse anonymisation when retained pointers cannot be shown non-identifying
open_points.default_guess: Require the owner to establish that retained pointers are non-identifying before choosing anonymisation; otherwise delete the project whole.
